__snake__cx: On the way to T-F23, Arno "Rabbit" Snake tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way.
Blackwater Canal is lost. Arno "Rabbit" Snake heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.

Arno "Rabbit" Snake tried to remember the sound of the church bell in Varenne. Every version sounded like the ration bell. Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Arno "Rabbit" Snake stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
angelogia55: Jonas "Doc" Angelogia arrived at R-F22 with a carefully folded uniform. The first low beam ruined the cap; the first puddle ruined the rest.

Jonas "Doc" Angelogia checked every ammunition belt by lamplight. One bad cartridge was enough to make him start the whole inspection again. A letter from home reached Jonas "Doc" Angelogia before dusk. Jonas "Doc" Angelogia read it twice and slept a little easier.

On sentry duty Jonas "Doc" Angelogia watched the wire for six hours. Twice he thought the wire watched back. Day 6. The Hegemony took Hill 304. From the heights Jonas "Doc" Angelogia could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
Jonas "Doc" Angelogia offered to read the newspaper aloud. The audience asked for the advertisements first, then the racing results, and the war last.
Jonas "Doc" Angelogia fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Yann "Brick" Zaza, grazed. Nobody nearby said anything.
Jonas "Doc" Angelogia had marked the corner of the enemy trench with two stakes in daylight. At night the gun fired between the stakes, blind. Konrad Nsrr was grazed.
Jonas "Doc" Angelogia fired short bursts at the gap in the enemy wire, the way the sergeant taught. Albin "Saint" Zaza was badly wounded trying to cross it.

The water jacket hissed as Jonas "Doc" Angelogia fired across no man's land. When the gun went quiet, Valentin "Mud" Chavo was badly wounded. The Hegemony flag went up over Blackwater Canal. Jonas "Doc" Angelogia did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.

Jonas "Doc" Angelogia taught Benedikt "Mole" Twenskyyy to play the harmonica. The whole squad has asked them both, politely, to stop. Jonas "Doc" Angelogia got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 287. The men who came later will ask about it. The Hegemony secured Grey Mill. Jonas "Doc" Angelogia helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.
azok_78046: Benedikt Azok arrived with the Day 9 draft, carrying a book with the last pages torn out and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.
Day 10: Blackwater Canal was lost. Benedikt Azok wrote down the news without trying to explain it.

Benedikt Azok wrote a letter home. He wrote about the weather. He did not write about the rats. Grey Mill is lost. Benedikt Azok heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.
chrisoostuizen: Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz introduced himself as a clockmaker from Belmonte. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz and Teodor Shadowizard have a secret signal: two taps on the helmet means 'still here'. They use it every night after the flares go out.

Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz made it into the enemy trench and out again, but a machine gun swept no man's land on the way home. Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz crawled the last yards. The Hegemony flag went up over Blackwater Canal. Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again. A letter from home found Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz before the night shift. Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz folded it small and kept it close.

Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz came back to the squad today. The men had kept his spot on the fire step and his spoon. A letter from home found Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz before the night shift. Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz folded it small and kept it close. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz is number 572. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. News that the Hegemony had taken Grey Mill reached Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
coffee_slayer: By the time Karel Slayer reached U-F8, the war was 11 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down. The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Grey Mill. Karel Slayer folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
donkay18035: Yann Donkay signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at P-F7 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word. The Hegemony took Grey Mill, and the orders at P-F7 changed before the cheering ended. Yann Donkay shouldered another load.
eliyork13: Bram Eliyork reported to U-F7 with a rosary of rough beads sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice. Grey Mill has been won. Bram Eliyork listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
euberitaminis: Day 6: Felix "Tin" Euberitamini reached R-S7 with a full packet of cigarettes. Learning everyone's name proved remarkably easy.

A crow sat on the parapet above Felix "Tin" Euberitamini all afternoon. The men say it chose him. A letter from home found Felix "Tin" Euberitamini before the night shift. Felix "Tin" Euberitamini folded it small and kept it close.
Felix "Tin" Euberitamini found an old map of the Ossuary Wood from before the war. There was a school on it, and an orchard. He looked for them. He did not find them.
Felix "Tin" Euberitamini tried to remember the price of a loaf in Dunmarrow. Three different answers seemed right, depending on how far back he thought.
Pavel "Tin" Satan of the Concord shouted a joke across the wire at the Hanging Bridge. Felix "Tin" Euberitamini of the Hegemony laughed before remembering not to. Both lines heard it.
Felix "Tin" Euberitamini walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.

Felix "Tin" Euberitamini had just lit a cigarette at R-S7 when a bullet cut a line across his cheek. He finished the cigarette before going to the medic. Shot by Nils Averelle of the Concord (@averelle_3d). A letter from home found Felix "Tin" Euberitamini before the night shift. Felix "Tin" Euberitamini folded it small and kept it close. Felix "Tin" Euberitamini got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 383. The men who came later will ask about it. The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Grey Mill. Felix "Tin" Euberitamini folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.
hazy_hero: Henrik "Ghost" Hero signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at U-F7 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word.

Henrik "Ghost" Hero gave Casimir Addicted the last match in the trench. Casimir used it to light a candle so that Ghost could finish a letter. Grey Mill is lost. Henrik "Ghost" Hero heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.
hunnery707: Florian Hunnery took the place of a man nobody would talk about. The dugout still had his blanket. He kept it folded.
Word came down the line: Blackwater Canal is ours. Florian Hunnery shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.

Florian Hunnery agreed to sit for a portrait drawn by a man with a piece of charcoal. The first result made him look twice his age. Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Florian Hunnery watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
jacobsoifu: Walter Jacobsoifu arrived on Day 9 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.
The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. Walter Jacobsoifu watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.

Walter Jacobsoifu was carrying water up to S-R6 when a bullet hit him in the leg. The water reached the trench. Walter Jacobsoifu did not. Shot by Gustav Chongo of the Hegemony (@big__chongo). Walter Jacobsoifu stood up to fix a loose sandbag at S-R6. He did not get to finish the job. Shot by Gustav Chongo of the Hegemony (@big__chongo).

Florian Jacobsoifu put a pressed cornflower beside the bunk. Someone who had known Walter Jacobsoifu helped clear the shelf without saying why. The clerk counted the names twice. Florian Jacobsoifu is number 905 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Grey Mill. Florian Jacobsoifu read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.
josh_t_polley: Tobias Polley arrived on Day 9 as a replacement. The men in Q-F15 had been fighting for 9 days already and looked at his clean boots like a rumour from another world.
From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Tobias Polley wrote to a sweetheart who has stopped writing that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'

Tobias Polley brushed dried mud off a letter and found one more word under it: 'soon'. He wished the rest of the sentence had survived. The Hegemony took Grey Mill. Tobias Polley watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.
no_one35643: In Kesselby, Karel "Doc" One was a tailor. In P-F16, he is a number and a rifle. He has told everyone he intends to be a tailor again. News that the Hegemony had taken Grey Mill reached Karel "Doc" One during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
zksoon1: Nobody saw Casimir Zksoon arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in R-S8, and a quiet rifleman under it.
Casimir Zksoon and Walter Markdavis carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident.
A shell hit the latrine at R-S8. Nobody was hurt. Casimir Zksoon says it was the best day of the war.
A scrap of newspaper advertised a sale of garden furniture. Casimir Zksoon worked out how many months of pay a comfortable afternoon would cost.
New laces made Casimir Zksoon's boots look almost respectable, until he stood up.
The sergeant read out the order: Blackwater Canal has fallen, hold the line. Casimir Zksoon looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.

Casimir Zksoon sharpened a pencil carefully and then could not think what to write. He put the date at the top anyway. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Casimir Zksoon is number 408. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. After the loss of Grey Mill, Casimir Zksoon helped stack spare sandbags at R-S8. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
